answer: An agent named willow runs a freight market linking a jetty to a mesa warehouse. Before bidding, each carrier buys a nontransferable capacity permit backed by locked collateral. Orders are assigned randomly, and payment requires matching signed pickup and arrival records from independent operators. Duplicate cargo identifiers earn no second payment; conflicting records freeze the permit for review. Splitting into many aliases cannot expand collateral-backed capacity, while fabricated deliveries risk both the bond and transport expenses.
